claims.text: Boron microalloying modifies the microstructure of a high-entropy-alloy coating.
Controlled thermal processing of the boron-modified AlCoCrFeNiMo-based coating creates a refined near-surface microstructure.
The modified coating forms in situ nanoscale TiB2 precipitates.
Dynamic amorphization produces or sustains a refined near-surface layer during mechanical deformation.
A dynamically generated ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer can contribute to low friction and high wear resistance in a high-entropy alloy.
Finely dispersed TiB2 particles create a dense, passivating surface structure.
The proposed dense surface structure minimizes the nucleation of corrosion sites.
Dynamic amorphization under mechanical stress continuously regenerates or maintains corrosion passivation.
Boron-induced microstructural changes are linked to improved wear and corrosion resistance in a coating.
The boron-modified, thermally processed alloy will have a lower wear rate than the baseline alloy.
The boron-modified, thermally processed alloy will exhibit a higher corrosion potential than the baseline alloy.
The boron-modified, thermally processed alloy will exhibit a lower corrosion current density than the baseline alloy.
The modification will improve resistance to simultaneous wear and corrosion in 3.5 wt.% NaCl.
Excessive TiB2 growth could impair passivation.
The predicted benefit may fail when the passive layer is unstable or when the alloy is overdoped with boron.
The cited dynamic-amorphization behavior is applicable from CoCrFeMnNi tested in ultra-high vacuum to an AlCoCrFeNiMo-based coating tested in saline tribocorrosion.

contradictions.description: The stated AlCoCrFeNiMo-based alloy contains no titanium and the intervention adds only boron, yet the mediator and mechanism require in situ TiB2 formation. No titanium source is specified.
